title: Braces and range-for for your own class
description:
Two small additions make a container class feel like part of the language.

1. A constructor taking `std::initializer_list<int>` lets callers write `IntList list{ 3, 1, 4 };`
2. `begin()` and `end()` let it be used in a range-based `for` loop. For a class that stores its elements in one array, plain pointers work as iterators: `begin()` points at the first element, `end()` one past the last.

Add both to `IntList` (const versions of `begin`/`end` too).
hints: Delegate to the size constructor with **round** brackets, `IntList(values.size())`. With braces the compiler would pick the initializer-list constructor again.
